body: I found which node is causing the issue and how to work around it.  I'll post an update tomorrow! :)

Okay here are the details of what the shader does, what I discovered the issue to be, and how I worked around it.

# Summary

I have this "eyes map" that instructs the shader where to "subtract" from in regards to albedo, emission, metallic, etc. so that the eyes are effectively a black void.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60077c4f-bc9a-4bf7-ab8d-bec641397ada)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2300294b-1974-476b-9c42-cb447f19a87f)

Here is the emission portion of the shader graph.  I've moved the other nodes out of the way for now so we can focus on the problematic section:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abd52215-a3f5-413a-a5c6-9b2e38641f85)

Now lets zoom in on the exact node that is causing our issues:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99e589db-7f32-4a4d-b2b0-a5669fbd02c6)

The "Vector3Scalar" node is used to remove the "eyes" from the emission map.  Executing the "Vector3Scalar" function on the emission map BEFORE doing the color and strength multiplication is the problem.  If I move this node to the end, everything works just fine.  Here is the updated graph:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d5b64df-8f20-4a84-aa4f-b05bb5126cd6)

By moving that to the end just before attaching to "Emission" everything works!  Here's a pic of a happy cube guy! :)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a9fb7f4-5c75-4f5b-af94-4a14bb85d4fd)

Now my next question for you awesome godot devs:

Why?  This seems like a bug as we are getting different visual behavior between desktop and mobile.  Is it a bug on the Godot side or Android and iOS sides?  A bug in those mobile drivers?  If it was just one or the other (i.e. Android or iOS) I would suspect a driver issue.  But because it is in both, this makes me think it is on the Godot side.  But inspecting the source code, it is not clear to me where.  Fortunately I have this workaround for this specific shader for now! :)

Let me know if anyone has any further questions :)  As always, thank you for the awesome engine! :)

It's tough to say from just that amount of information. My gut feeling is that you are running into some undefined behaviour in GLSL so you are getting different results from different drivers. Godot generates the same code from visual shaders regardless of the platform. So the fact that you get different results points to this being an issue with how the code is compiled/executed by the graphics driver on your device. Desktop drivers tend to be more forgiving to mistakes in shader code while mobile drivers tend to be more punishing. 

I would double check your inputs to that bit of shader code to ensure you don't have any cases of negative numbers, NaNs, INFs, or unexpected `0`s
